disasters.summary: Super Typhoon Champi (Rosal) formed on 11 October 2026 and passed near Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the Philippines, Taiwan and Okinawa, Japan. It became extratropical on 25 October and dissipated on 27 October. Reported impacts include one death and 616+ injured in Taiwan, damaged homes on Guam, power cuts in Okinawa, and at least US$7.86 million in economic damage.

disasters.summary: A M7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County, Nagqu, Xizang (Tibet), China, on 22 October 2026 at 14:33 UTC. Sixteen people were killed and 76 injured as of 24 October. Search and rescue is reported complete, with no people missing. As of 27 October, relief efforts and aftershocks were still being reported, and the affected railway section had resumed normal service.

disasters.summary: Hurricane Vance, a cyclone that started on 21 October 2026, is now a weakening tropical storm offshore from Mexico's Pacific coast, according to the National Hurricane Center bulletin issued 27 October 2026 at 08:00 MST. It has 35-knot winds and is expected to turn north toward the entrance of the Gulf of California by Thursday. No land impacts have been reported. Mexican authorities have taken preventive measures in five Pacific states.

disasters.summary: Prolonged drought is affecting parts of Central America, which began on 21 April 2026. On 24 October 2026 the IFRC said about one million people in Honduras are affected. A red alert covers 103 Honduran municipalities, and 234 more are under other alert levels. Drought is projected to worsen between October 2026 and March 2027. Western Nicaragua and southeastern Mexico also report dry conditions.

disasters.summary: A drought affecting parts of East Africa and the Central Sahel is ongoing as of 25 October 2026. A Red Cross plan issued 12 October says the trigger for action was met on 1 September 2026. Reported impacts include about 250,035 hectares of cropland damaged in Ethiopia and a warning from the IPC of famine risk in Sudan's Darfur and Kordofan regions. The start date of 21 June 2026 is not confirmed by any source found.

disasters.summary: Kanlaon Volcano in the Philippines had a moderately explosive eruption on 10 October 2026 at about 12:46 p.m. PHIVOLCS recorded ash emissions on 11 October and kept Alert Level 2. Ash fell in several Negros Occidental towns. Around 24,000 families were affected, and residents within a 4 km radius of the permanent danger zone evacuated. The latest reports found are from 12 October; no later reports were found.

disasters.summary: Taal Volcano in Batangas, Philippines, had a minor phreatomagmatic eruption on 8 October 2026, causing ashfall and evacuations in Agoncillo. Further minor eruptions followed on 20 and 22 October, sending plumes of up to 1,200 metres. The 26 October bulletin kept Alert Level 1. Evacuees were advised not to return home immediately because of sulfur odours and safety concerns.

Water assessments and holding centres were still active in the latest IFRC report, dated 11 October 2026, and some roads remained cut off.

No later source was found on the current status.

disasters.summary: Monsoon depression rains and flash floods hit Cox's Bazar and other districts in Bangladesh from early July 2026, with landslides and waterlogging. Cox's Bazar's Rohingya camps were among the hardest hit. The UN reported 59 deaths and the Joint Needs Assessment of 29 July reported 1.28 million people affected. The latest source found, IFRC GO updated 20 August 2026, lists the operation running to 31 January 2027. No source reports the flooding has ended.
